run.note: Scoped pass over the releases since the 2.9.0 full pass: 2.9.1, 2.10.0-2.10.3. Five new items cover the 2.10.x watch fixes.

findings-against-prior-runs: The 2.9.0 run listed EventId 1005 among emitted ids without remark. It is the embed drain failing on a bank with no embedding engine set: each pass logs a Warning with a full ArgumentOutOfRangeException stack ('Unknown embedding provider; expected local or openai'). Seen on 2.10.1-2.10.3 scratch banks until 'model embedding set local'. Not a defect of an item, but noisy on every fresh install.
The 2.9.0 run's watch-catch-up evidence ('get_watch_status reads Healthy') holds only for watches whose catch-up digested a file; idle watches with nothing due stay Scanning after a restart (#971).
The 2.10.3 changelog says a notebook cell with an unpaired surrogate escape no longer fails its watch; it still does (#970).

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory (`settings ingest scope add`, `settings watch enable`, add_watch) holding x.md, w.md and y.md, plus node_modules/pkg/index.md and .git/notes.md, each with a term found nowhere else. Wait for three watch_files rows and leave node_modules readable (a `chmod 000` decoy is absent whether or not it is excluded, so that leg could never fail), wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds query finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and get_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)
items.command: Scratch dir wF with x.md (quillfernab), w.md (marbleqrs), y.md, node_modules/pkg/index.md (nodemodtermqa); add_watch; wait for 3 watch_files rows; edit y.md; read updated_at/last_change_ts while the server runs; kill server 51485; same-length swap quillfernab->emberwolfxy in x.md, touch to 1795201925; rewrite w.md 21->41 bytes (glimmerashq), touch to 1795201920; serve again on the same data root and port 54828; poll query; watch_files; get_watch_status
items.evidence:
premise: x.md updated_at 1795201924, mtime 1795201925 after touch, last_change_ts 1795201927 -> updated_at <= mtime <= last_change_ts; w.md mtime 1795201920 < updated_at 1795201924; sizes x 26->26, w 21->41
before restart: quillfernab and marbleqrs FOUND, nodemodtermqa NOTFOUND
after restart: FOUND emberwolfxy after 0.7s; FOUND glimmerashq after 0.1s; NOTFOUND nodemodtermqa within 3.0s
watch_files: w.md|1795201955|41, x.md|1795201955|26, y.md|1795201927|30
get_watch_status wF: Healthy
items.observed-result: Restart catch-up found both missed edits (the same-size x.md by its own fingerprint, the backdated w.md by size) and the watch read Healthy; the node_modules term was never found.
items.acceptance-reason: Matches ADR-0121. The dot-git decoy leg was not driven: this session's environment guard blocks writing a .git directory, and the auto-mode classifier denied a workaround. The 5-minute heal pass was not waited for (optional).

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory whose root holds ai-raccoon.ignore (excluding skip/) plus a.md with a unique term. After the initial scan settles, the serve log gains no EventId 899 line for 30 s, and watch_files keeps the ignore file with a 64-hex file_hash. Append a rule to ai-raccoon.ignore: exactly one rescan follows (the 899 or digest lines appear once, then stop again for 30 s). (ADR-0154)
items.command: MCP add_watch $S/w/wA (ai-raccoon.ignore = 'skip/', a.md fernquiltax, skip/s.md skipdirzx); wait 8 s; count serve log lines for 30 s idle; sqlite3 -readonly watch_files for the ignore file; edit ignore to 'skip/\nnone/' and watch 30 s; then set ignore to 'none/' (skip/ now indexable), poll query skipdirzx and read the log for 30 s more. Control: same tree on 2.10.2 (scratch --tool-path, data root d2) for 30 s idle and after an ignore edit.
items.evidence:
2.10.3 30 s idle: no new log lines at all
watch_files: wA/ai-raccoon.ignore|4882cacefde9bfbc9721b3c42945687df9261da9244159959c925a025c5bae2c|6
after adding none/: 0 log lines in 30 s; row -> 9aebea873d0000d7...|12|1795201562
after removing skip/: FOUND skipdirzx after 2.0s; log: one SqliteMemoryStore[899] 'Replace-by-path ... (1 row(s) written)', then quiet for 30 s
2.10.2 control: 30 s idle no 899 lines; after an ignore edit exactly one 899 '(0 row(s) written)', then quiet
items.observed-result: On 2.10.3 an unchanged ignore file starts no rescan, the ignore row keeps a 64-hex hash, and an edit that frees a directory starts exactly one rescan that indexes it. The 2.10.2 control did not loop on macOS either, so the quiet window is not a discriminating check on this host; the one-rescan-per-edit leg is.
items.acceptance-reason: Expected behaviour observed on 2.10.3. The loop was reported on Windows; this run could not reproduce it on 2.10.2/macOS, and the item's negative control now says so.
items.negative-control: Remove a rule so that an excluded file becomes indexable: exactly one rescan indexes it, which shows the edit is seen. A 2.10.2 build on macOS (2026-11-20) did not reproduce the loop in 30 s, so the quiet window alone is not proof on macOS; the loop was reported on Windows.

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory holding bin.md (an indexed extension with NUL bytes, which ingest skips) and good.md. watch_files keeps a row for bin.md whose file_hash starts with `skip:`, and over 30 s idle the serve log gains no digest of bin.md. Rewrite bin.md: it is digested once and stays skip-marked. good.md's term is found by query. (ADR-0153)
items.command: MCP add_watch $S/w/wB (bin.md with NUL bytes, good.md goodmarkqv); sqlite3 -readonly watch_files; 30 s idle log; get_watch_status; query goodmarkqv; restart server (same data root) and read watch_files + 30 s idle log again. Control: same tree on 2.10.1 (scratch --tool-path, data root d3).
items.evidence:
2.10.3 watch_files: wB/bin.md|skip:aabf7fd0299ad1ee566e0b9eca9d5f992084a69f795437a273725af24f6bab15|21
get_watch_status wB: Healthy, skippedCount 1, skipped [{path: .../wB/bin.md, reason: binary}]
30 s idle: no log lines; FOUND goodmarkqv after 0.1s
after restart: wB/bin.md|skip:aabf7fd0299ad1e|1795201955 (retried once at start), then 30 s idle: no log lines
2.10.1 control watch_files: ai-raccoon.ignore, a.md, data.json, good.md -- no row for bin.md; wB skippedCount 1
items.observed-result: 2.10.3 keeps a skip-marked stamp for the skipped file, lists it as skipped, and does not digest it again while idle; after a restart it is retried once and stays skip-marked. 2.10.1 keeps no stamp for the same file.
items.acceptance-reason: Matches ADR-0153. The rewrite leg was not driven separately; the restart retry shows a due skipped file is digested once.
items.negative-control: Same tree served by 2.10.1 from a scratch --tool-path keeps no watch_files row for bin.md (2.10.3 keeps a skip: row).

items.expected-result: Watch a scratch directory holding data.json whose property name is the escape \uD83D, and nb.ipynb and hi.ipynb whose markdown cell sources hold \uDE00 and \uD83D, each next to a unique term. With the memory and code engines set, get_watch_status reads Healthy with no lastError, and query finds every term. When a digest does fail, lastError starts with the file's path. (ADR-0154)
items.command: model embedding set local + model code set default (--port); write wC/d2.json {"\uD83D": "surrmarkjw2", ...} and wC/nb.ipynb (markdown cell source 'nbcellmarkqz \uDE00 tail'); new watch wG/hi.ipynb (source 'hicellmarkqz \uD83D tail'); get_watch_status; query each term (entryType file,code); serve log WatchPipeline[304]. Control: same files on 2.10.2.
items.evidence:
2.10.3: FOUND surrmarkjw2 after 0.1s; NOTFOUND nbcellmarkqz within 3.0s
wC Retrying '.../w/wC/nb.ipynb: Cannot read invalid UTF-16 JSON text as string. Invalid surrogate value: '0xDE00'.'
wG Retrying '.../w/wG/hi.ipynb: Cannot read incomplete UTF-16 JSON text as string with missing low surrogate.'
warn: AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Watch.WatchPipeline[304] Watch digest of .../nb.ipynb failed
  at System.Text.Json.JsonReaderHelper.GetUnescapedString(...)
  at AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Chunking.NotebookChunker.Source(JsonElement cell)
  at AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Chunking.NotebookChunker.Flatten(String text)
2.10.2 control: wC Retrying 'Cannot read invalid UTF-16 JSON text as string. Invalid surrogate value: '0xDE00'.' (no path)
items.observed-result: The JSON-file leg indexes. A notebook cell with a lone surrogate (high or low) still fails its whole watch on 2.10.3: NotebookChunker.Source throws in System.Text.Json before the tokenizer fix applies. The 2.10.3 lastError now names the file (2.10.2 did not).
items.acceptance-reason: Defect tracked in #970. The 2.10.3 changelog claims the notebook case is fixed. Acceptance is the owner's decision.
items.negative-control: Same tree served by 2.10.2 from a scratch --tool-path: lastError holds the message without the file path.

items.expected-result: add_watch over MCP on a scratch directory with a unique term: query finds the term within 5 s, not after the 10 s reconcile interval. remove_watch, then create a new file with a second unique term: it is never found within 20 s. (ADR-0152)
items.command: MCP add_watch {projectId, path: $S/w/wD2} (wD2/d.md holds addmarkwq), then poll MCP query addmarkwq (entryType file, vectorWeight 0) every 0.25 s; MCP remove_watch wD2; write wD2/n.md (removedmarkkt) and, as a control, wD/c.md (controlmarkgv) on a still-watched dir; poll both 20 s; sqlite3 -readonly watch_files where path like '%wD2%'
items.evidence:
add_watch reply after 0.06s: {"data":{"projectId":"01a1fa57-...","path":".../w/wD2"...
FOUND addmarkwq after 0.2s (0.4s since add_watch call)
remove_watch -> {"data":{..."path":".../w/wD2","removed":true...
FOUND controlmarkgv after 0.7s
NOTFOUND removedmarkkt within 20.0s
watch_files rows for wD2 after remove: none
items.observed-result: The new watch indexed its file 0.4 s after the add_watch call, well under the 10 s reconcile interval. After remove_watch a new file in that directory was not indexed in 20 s, while a new file in a still-watched directory was indexed in 0.7 s.
items.acceptance-reason: Add applies at once (0.4 s < 5 s) and remove stops the watcher; the control proves the watcher was still working.
items.negative-control: Time the add from the add_watch reply to the first hit; record the elapsed time, since a build without the wake signal takes up to 10 s.

items.expected-result: On a watched scratch directory, add a rule for later/ to ai-raccoon.ignore, then create later/n.md with a unique term: query never finds it within 20 s. Create kept/k.md with another term in the same window: query finds it. (ADR-0151, ADR-0152)
items.command: MCP add_watch $S/w/wE (e.md edirmarkqp); write ai-raccoon.ignore 'later/'; after 2 s create later/n.md (latermarkvb) and kept/k.md (keptmarkhd); poll query 20 s each; sqlite3 -readonly watch_files for wE
items.evidence:
FOUND edirmarkqp after 0.7s
FOUND keptmarkhd after 1.2s
NOTFOUND latermarkvb within 20.0s
watch_files: wE/ai-raccoon.ignore, wE/e.md, wE/kept/k.md (no later/n.md)
items.observed-result: A rule added to the ignore file applies to files created after it; the control file in a non-ignored directory was indexed in the same window.
items.acceptance-reason: Matches ADR-0151/0152; the control proves the watcher was live.
items.negative-control: kept/k.md is the control: a watcher that stopped processing would also not find later/n.md.

items.expected-result: Seed distinguishable Memory/File/Code plus an unclassified control. Drive all seven nonempty entryType subsets and omitted default, including mixed case/spacing. Narrow sets return only declared selected types; any selection naming both memory and file (default/all included) also returns unclassified rows. Confirm kind_mask exactly 1..7. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0141)

items.observed-result: Narrow selections return only their declared kinds; every selection naming both memory and file (and the default) also returns the unclassified row; kind_mask values are exactly 1..7.
items.acceptance-reason: Matches the 2.9.1 wording. Before the re-embed, 'memory' also returned the unclassified row through the vector leg because a hand-unclassified row keeps its old vector partition; that is a substrate artifact of the seeding, not product behaviour.

items.expected-result: In full access mode set/clear Memory TTL; refuse setting and clearing File, unclassified and Code-only hashes, and retain negative controls. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0148, ADR-0150)

full; set_memory_ttl set/clear on Memory, File, unclassified and Code hashes and an unknown hash; sqlite3 -readonly entries.ttl_days after each
